tagline: Snap a crop leaf. Diagnose diseases. Get authoritative treatment advice.

Healthy.name: Healthy Crop Leaf
Healthy.summary: The leaf shows healthy chloroplast pigmentation, uniform cellular turgor, and zero pathogen lesions or chlorotic mottling.
management: No curative treatment needed.
Maintain regular irrigation, ensuring well-drained root-zone conditions without waterlogging.
Apply balanced NPK fertilization tailored to soil fertility analysis.
prevention: Rotate fields every season with non-host crops to disrupt soil-borne pathogens.
Perform routine visual scouts once weekly, especially during humid spells.
Healthy.chemicalGuidance: No chemical intervention needed. Preserve beneficial natural microorganisms on the foliage.
Healthy.safetyDisclaimer: Avoid unneeded chemical sprays to protect helpful field insects and soil health.

Early Leaf Spot.name: Early Leaf Spot (Cercospora)
Early Leaf Spot.summary: Subcircular necrotic lesions (1-10 mm) on leaf surface bordered by prominent chlorotic yellow halos, active under sustained humidity.
management: Maintain adequate plant spacing to improve airflow through the crop canopy.
Rogue and safely destroy heavily infected bottom leaves during initial focal outbreaks.
Foliar spray with 5% Neem Seed Kernel Extract (NSKE) or Trichoderma harzianum formulation.
prevention: Sow certified seeds treated with Trichoderma viride @ 4 g/kg or Thiram @ 3 g/kg seed.
Practice deep summer ploughing to bury old crop stubble and resting spores.
Follow a two-year crop rotation cycle with non-host crops.
Early Leaf Spot.chemicalGuidance: Spray Mancozeb 75% WP @ 1000 g/ha (2-2.5 g/L water) or Carbendazim 50% WP @ 500 g/ha (1 g/L water) every 10-14 days upon early symptom onset.
Early Leaf Spot.safetyDisclaimer: Use only locally registered fungicides. Strictly observe 15-day pre-harvest intervals and wear safety masks during application.

Late Leaf Spot.name: Late Leaf Spot (Phaeoisariopsis)
Late Leaf Spot.summary: Dark brown to carbon-black circular lesions predominantly on the lower leaf surface, with minimal yellow halos, causing rapid canopy defoliation.
management: Avoid night-time sprinkler irrigation which extends nocturnal leaf wetness periods.
Collect and destroy diseased crop debris post-harvest to reduce overwintering spore reservoirs.
Foliar bio-control spray with Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 2.5 kg/ha in 500 L water.
prevention: Select disease-tolerant crop cultivars recommended by national research institutes.
Balance NPK fertilization; avoid excess nitrogen that creates dense, disease-prone canopies.
Late Leaf Spot.chemicalGuidance: Spray Hexaconazole 5% EC @ 1000 ml/ha (2 ml/L water) or Chlorothalonil 75% WP @ 1000 g/ha (2 g/L) or Tebuconazole 25.9% EC @ 500-750 ml/ha.
Late Leaf Spot.safetyDisclaimer: Wear protective chemical gloves and mask. Observe pre-harvest intervals.

Rust.name: Foliar Rust Disease
Rust.summary: Dense clusters of raised reddish-brown pustules that rupture into powdery masses of airborne spores, causing curling, scorch, and heavy yield drop.
management: Remove and safely burn severely infected plants from isolated infection foci.
Drain standing water immediately from field furrows to reduce humidity.
prevention: Adopt rust-resistant or tolerant crop cultivars certified by agricultural universities.
Intercrop with tall cereals (sorghum, maize at 3:1 row ratio) as physical spore barrier crops.
Rust.chemicalGuidance: Spray Tebuconazole 25.9% EC @ 500-750 ml/ha (1-1.5 ml/L water) or Propiconazole 25% EC @ 500 ml/ha (1 ml/L water).
Rust.safetyDisclaimer: Wear protective chemical gloves and face mask during application. Observe pre-harvest withholding safety periods.

Black Spot.name: Black Spot Disease
Black Spot.scientificName: Diplocarpon rosae Wolf / Septoria foliar complex
Black Spot.summary: Circular black spots with feathery or fringed borders surrounded by bright yellow chlorosis, causing progressive leaf drop and cane defoliation.
management: Prune and safely discard all infected leaves and fallen debris; do not allow infected foliage to overwinter.
Prune lower stems to improve air circulation and prevent soil-splash spore transmission.
Switch strictly to ground-level or drip irrigation in the morning hours so foliage dries quickly.
prevention: Select certified disease-tolerant varieties adapted to regional humidity.
Apply bio-fungicidal sprays with Bacillus subtilis or potassium bicarbonate solutions early in season.
Ensure generous spacing between plants to maximize sunlight exposure.
Black Spot.chemicalGuidance: Spray Chlorothalonil 75% WP @ 2 g/L or Myclobutanil 10% WP @ 1 g/L or Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.5 g/L at 10-14 day intervals during damp conditions.
Black Spot.safetyDisclaimer: Wear chemical safety gloves and goggles. Avoid midday applications in strong sun to prevent foliar scorching.

Downy Mildew - Mosaic.name: Downy Mildew & Mosaic Complex
Downy Mildew - Mosaic.summary: Angular chlorotic patches bounded by leaf veins on upper leaf surfaces, with purplish-gray downy sporulation underneath, accompanied by mosaic vein clearing.
management: Remove severely infected foliage immediately and dispose away from the field.
Water exclusively at soil level through drip lines to eliminate leaf wetness windows.
Manage sap-sucking insect vectors (aphids, whiteflies) with yellow sticky traps and 5% neem oil sprays.
prevention: Plant certified hybrid cultivars with documented downy mildew and viral tolerance.
Eradicate wild weed hosts along field boundaries that harbor viral pathogens.
Maintain minimum 3-year crop rotation with non-cucurbit crops.
Downy Mildew - Mosaic.chemicalGuidance: Foliar spray with Metalaxyl 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP @ 2.5 g/L or Cymoxanil 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP @ 2 g/L or Copper Oxychloride 50% WP @ 3 g/L.
Downy Mildew - Mosaic.safetyDisclaimer: Rotate chemical families (FRAC groups) to prevent fungicide resistance. Observe pre-harvest withholding intervals.

Nutrition Deficiency.name: Foliar Nutrient Deficiency
Nutrition Deficiency.summary: Interveinal chlorosis, generalized leaf yellowing, or apical margin scorching caused by essential macro/micronutrient shortages in the root zone.
management: Spray Ferrous Sulphate (FeSO4) @ 0.5% (5 g/L) + Citric Acid (1 g/L) twice at 10-day intervals for iron chlorosis.
Apply balanced 19:19:19 water-soluble NPK foliar spray @ 5 g/L for general vigor recovery.
Side-dress appropriate soil amendments (gypsum, compost) based on soil test results.
prevention: Perform annual soil testing before planting to establish accurate baseline pH and nutrient profiles.
Incorporate well-decomposed farmyard manure or vermicompost @ 10-12 t/ha during soil preparation.
Avoid over-irrigation which leaches vital mobile nutrients past the root absorption zone.
Nutrition Deficiency.chemicalGuidance: Use specialized water-soluble micronutrient and fertilizer supplements. Do not apply chemical fungicides for physiological yellowing.
Nutrition Deficiency.safetyDisclaimer: Observe recommended dilution concentrations. Excessively concentrated foliar fertilizer sprays burn leaf margins.
